To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel fast-approximated (FAT) triplet loss and label distillation strategy, which can be combined to learn robust person ReID features.

the triplet loss is a powerful loss for learning ReID features, that can be extended to large scale datasets and be robust to noisy labels by approximating its upper bound form (the fast approximated triplet loss) and by using a label distillation strategy.

(a) the proposed fast approximated triplet loss is an upper bound of the triplet loss and thus preserves the effectiveness of the triplet loss, while having linear time and memory complexity with respect to the number of samples; (b) the proposed label distillation strategy can learn robust soft labels from a small subset of confident samples and can be used to train a teacher network to generate refined soft labels for training a student network; (c) the proposed FAT loss with distilled label leads to ReID features
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two aspects: 1) How to improve the accuracy, efficiency and robustness of person re-identification with the triplet loss?
the following two aspects: (1) How can we learn robust ReID features from large-scale ReID data?

the following three aspects: (i) the triplet loss is a good choice for person re-identification, (ii) the triplet loss can be approximated to a computationally cheaper loss, and (iii) the triplet loss and the approximated loss can be used with noisy labels, and can be used for label distillation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the triplet loss is a good loss function to learn person re-identification features.
the proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art results on the three benchmarks, and is the most efficient approach to date.
the triplet loss is not dead, and is in fact a very good loss for learning robust person ReID features, and it can be made even better with our proposed FAT loss and label distillation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the triplet loss is indeed a powerful choice for learning robust ReID features, even in the presence of massive data and label noise.
we have developed a fast-approximate triplet loss with label distillation strategy, which is more effective and efficient for ReID feature learning.

, with only a few examples, the proposed FAT loss with label distillation is able to learn robust ReID features that can generalize to unseen domains, with a much higher speed than existing triplet-based losses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
triplet losses can be used to train robust ReID features with fast convergence and direct transferability, without the need to use any extra data augmentation or model ensemble techniques.
the triplet loss is not only a competitive loss for learning ReID features but also a more robust choice than the classification loss in the presence of label noise.
, the proposed FAT loss is a promising candidate for learning robust and transferable ReID features, with its efficiency, effectiveness, and direct generalizability to unseen data.
